# Cedric Stanhope

## Overview

- **Age:** Nineteen years old (at the time of Nell's wedding)
- **Gender:** Male
- **Origin:** The United States (Boston)
- **Role:** Student and poet

## Appearance

As a young child of ten, Cedric appeared small for his age with a delicate face, dark blue eyes, crimson lips, and chestnut curls. As he grew into his teenage years, he lost his curls for short-cut brown hair and grew significantly tall, eventually reaching six feet in height like his father.

## Personality

Cedric possesses a grave, meditative, and imaginative nature, often seeing the world through rich fantasies and dream-people such as the Rock People. He is polite, sensitive, and extraordinarily thoughtful toward others. He maintains strong sense of fairness and deep patriotic pride, while remaining fiercely dedicated and affectionate to those he loves.

## Traits

- Imaginative and poetic
- Polite and well-mannered
- Fear of the dark when going to sleep as a young child
- Fair and broad-minded

## Abilities

- Writing poetry
- Athletic skills and football

## Goals

- To grow up strong and reach his father's height
- To pursue two years of study abroad

## History

Cedric Stanhope arrived from the States to live with his grandmother in Brierley and attend the local school taught by Nell Harcourt. He quickly formed a deep bond of friendship with Nell, whom he loved dearly as a teacher. Though quiet and dreamy, he proved capable in schoolyard games and held his ground in a fight against St. Clair Trask over national pride. Cedric introduced Nell to his imaginative world of 'Rock People' on the beach, as well as his love for poetry. When Nell introduced Cedric to Miss Rosalind Penrose, his strong resemblance to his father Stephen Stanhope helped rekindle the past connection between Rosalind and Stephen. After his father returned and married Rosalind, Cedric moved to Boston to live with them, though he returned to Echo Cottage and Brierley during summer vacations. Over the years he grew into a tall young man, played football, and began publishing poetry in magazines. At nineteen, he returned to attend Nell's wedding before making plans to travel overseas for two years of study.

## Background by volume

- Son of Stephen Stanhope and his deceased first wife
- Raised partly in the States before coming to reside with his grandmother Stanhope on the shore road in Brierley
